Two concrete defects (tested against HEAD, then with the fix in a scratch copy, where import-test.js passes: 16/16 identical, 44 negatives, 131 checks, 0 failures).
(1) A top-level selection that is no known one is silently accepted when its entry id is an Object.prototype name, because T = D.bsIds is a plain object literal and T.info[id] is then inherited. 6 bigs with sels.unshift({id:'q', name:'Knight Castellan', entryId:'aaaa::constructor', number:1, type:'upgrade'}) imports (OK knight-destrier×2, knight-errant, knight-paladin×2, knight-warden). Adding a child {name:'Knight Castellan', entryId:'zz::toString', type:'model'} under an entry 'aaaa::hasOwnProperty' imports too, because T.infoKids is inherited the same way. That breaks “every other top-level selection … with known choices only” and the owner's rule that anything else is refused. A catalogueId of 'constructor' also hits T.factions.constructor and ends in “it could not be read” instead of “faction … not recognized”. The fix makes null-prototype copies of the tables. Both inputs are then refused with “selection Knight Castellan not recognized” / “selection Extra not recognized”, and the catalogue one with “faction Imperial Knights not recognized”.
(2) “A unit taken again as its copies” fails when the same unit comes from two lists of the pool. princes with its second Daemon Prince of Khorne swapped for a third Forgefiend (1910 pts) imports as forgefiend ×2 plus a separate forgefiend-2. picks reuses princes' Forgefiend up to its copies:2, then takes standard's Forgefiend (same detachments, so it is in the pool). The two are different objects, so `made` (keyed by object) does not merge them. They are identical field for field (JSON equal apart from copies). The fix keys `made` by the unit's JSON without copies, giving forgefiend ×3. (6 bigs with a third Knight Destrier merges only because no other IK list has a Destrier.)
